source_state: Uncommitted accumulated tank-driving work; source overlay against base identifies this pass.
notes: Wheel support uses actual wheelbase grade and upright chassis within 40 degrees, plus real upward native contacts under the chassis. Rigid support is unchanged.
Wheel default torque changes from 90 to 120. Radius 0.65, mass, top speed 2.5, acceleration 5, suspension and brake torque 120 remain unchanged.
Course CPU/held pass flat, step, slope and returned rubble at 120 in both shapes. CPU and goal refuse the trench. Physical torque-90 stalls remain despite repaired support.
Course forks follow 120 neutral settling ticks. Each report shares one physical start across all five branches. Different torque reports use separately initialized worlds.

Frozen reports retain the old-support goal controller and world at first false rejection. Neither native contacts nor best-distance/retry history is reset. Only selected-tank support changes in each old/new pair.

At torque 120 most frozen slow failures remain mechanically stuck even under held input; fixing support is not evidence that any blocked state can resume. Neutral controls expose rollback from these contact configurations.
Frozen torque-135 rubble goal reaches the destination in both shapes; torque-135 slope does not. Long held continuations may leave the course and lose support after the finish.
Goal speed/controller remains unchanged and headless. Fresh torque-120 slope/rubble goal attempts still exhaust retries. Normal gameplay CPU retains its range and aiming policies.
Rubble largely redeposits during the 120-tick warmup. This is a returned-rough-ground check, not a sustained loose-grain traction study.
Six --reference-support comparisons exactly reproduce previous native starts and all five final observation hashes, including goal histories, at explicit 90/120/135 torque.

All 26 existing benchmarks pass conservation and replay. Fourteen rigid/scripted hashes remain identical; twelve wheel hashes change with support/tuning. Incidental whole-scene timings are not evidence of a performance change.

The twenty course reports use the final physics. A later diagnostic-only edit fixes the old-support initial supported field and adds a report note; final-binary slope-120 and rubble-120 repeats match all trial values.
No production recovery AI or shared terrain behavior changes in this pass. No PR or commit created.
